title: Prediction versus in-sample fit
summary: R² describes how well a model explains the data it was estimated on; whether it predicts new cases must be assessed out of sample, without letting test data leak into estimation.

body.text: Explaining and predicting are different goals (Shmueli 2010). [[in-sample-fit]] measures such as R² use the same data for estimation and evaluation; they rise with model complexity and can overstate how well the model will do on new cases. [[out-of-sample-prediction]] estimates the model on training data and evaluates it on cases it has not seen.

[[plspredict]] (Shmueli et al. 2016, 2019) does this with k-fold cross-validation. For each indicator of an endogenous construct it reports Q²predict, which compares the prediction errors with those of the naive training-sample mean (positive values beat the mean), and RMSE or MAE compared with a linear-regression benchmark that ignores the construct structure. [[cvpat]] (Liengaard et al. 2021) tests whether one model's out-of-sample loss is significantly lower than another's.

SEM Studio does not compute PLSpredict or CVPAT yet (they are planned). The Q² from blindfolding is not an out-of-sample measure either: it omits data points within the estimation sample (Shmueli et al. 2016). To assess prediction now, use dedicated R packages.
body.title: Not available in SEM Studio

body.text: [[data-leakage]] happens when information from the evaluation cases influences the model: choosing items or paths after looking at the full sample, standardising or imputing with statistics computed on all data, or repeating the cross-validation with different settings until the numbers look good. Leakage makes out-of-sample results as optimistic as in-sample ones.

mistake.title: Claiming predictive power from R²
mistake.text: A high R² shows in-sample explanation. Statements such as "the model predicts intention well" require out-of-sample evidence such as PLSpredict, with a benchmark.

checks.question: An indicator of BI has Q²predict = .21 in a PLSpredict run. What does that mean?

options.text: The PLS model's out-of-sample predictions for that indicator have smaller errors than predicting with the training-sample mean.
options.feedback: Correct. Q²predict > 0 means the model beats the naive mean benchmark.

options.text: The model explains 21% of the variance of BI.
options.feedback: That would be an in-sample R²-type statement; Q²predict is a relative prediction-error measure.

options.text: The model predicts better than a linear regression benchmark.
options.feedback: That comparison uses RMSE or MAE against the LM benchmark, not Q²predict.

checks.explanation: Q²predict compares with the naive mean.

checks.question: Which procedure leaks test information into training?

options.text: Dropping items with low loadings in the full sample and then running a cross-validation on the reduced model.
options.feedback: Correct. The item selection already used the cases that later serve as test folds.

options.text: Fixing the model from theory, then running 10-fold cross-validation once.
options.feedback: Nothing about the held-out folds influenced the model or its settings.

options.text: Reporting in-sample R² next to out-of-sample metrics, clearly labelled.
options.feedback: Reporting both is fine as long as their meaning is clear.

checks.explanation: Any decision informed by the test cases is leakage.
